scenes.text: Every freelance developer knows this moment. A client asks: how much will it cost?
A local bakery wants online ordering. You list ten features, put one number next to each, add twenty percent, and hope. When a task blows up, you work the difference for free.
Scopecast quotes fixed-price work with a confidence level you choose.
Paste the client's feature list. Each line becomes a task, and bullets and numbering are cleaned up for you.
Instead of one number, every task gets a range. Type the likely hours and say how familiar the work is. Known work stays tight. New territory gets a long tail.

Scopecast runs the project ten thousand times. At eighty percent confidence, eight thousand of those runs finish within a hundred and forty-two hours. That is your price. Drag the dial, and you see exactly what certainty costs.
The client's budget is nine and a half thousand euros. Scopecast doesn't shave hours to make it fit. It finds the smallest set of tasks to move to a phase two, so the quote still holds.
Then it writes the quote your client reads: the scope, a fixed price, delivery in working days, phase two as an option, and one honest paragraph on how the price was estimated.

It was planned with the Devpost Learn skill pack: a scope, a product spec and a technical spec before any code. Then it was built in verified slices, with twenty-eight tests and a browser check for every step.
Scopecast. Quote a price you can stand behind.
